newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Slight disappointment at the Bank of Spain's decision to leave its rate unchanged was counterbalanced in the afternoon by further evidence of tame US inflation, due to a surprise reduction in January PPI.
Spain's bonos closed higher, although the long-term contract remained below key resistance at 115, while the 10-year spread over Bunds was almost untouched at 116 bps from 115 bps.

A volatile Italian market was adding pressure, as dealers said in the coming week EMU jitters could be back plaguing both the bonos and the peseta. The peseta strengthened after dealers said the Bank of Spain intervened.
In the money market the decision on unchanged rate brought a sharp rise in day-to-day rates, with overnight money ending at 6.10/20 percent from 5.80/90 yesterday.
"People were not really expecting an official rate cut, but now they are unwinding positions and this will also depress prices in the longer end of the yield curve," a dealer said.
The peseta's instability, considered by dealers as a major factor in the Bank of Spain's decision, was limited today by intervention.
But the yield curve flattened with the two-to-10 year spread falling to 122 basis points from 136 bps.
